comparison: Perfect claim overlap (C52-C54) regarding puncta formation after cholesterol depletion. OpenEval rated as UNCERTAIN noting the interpretation is speculative without determining puncta nature. Peer reviewers also rated UNCERTAIN, concerned the observation could confuse readers and requested clarification that puncta are likely D4 aggregates. Both agree the interpretation requires additional explanation.

High claim overlap (C2, C10-C13) on background context about cholesterol distribution consensus and Liu et al.'s contrasting findings. Both rated SUPPORTED. OpenEval found the literature summary accurate and appropriate. Peer reviewers accepted this framing without challenge, acknowledging Liu et al.'s findings contradict published studies. Strong agreement on contextual accuracy.

Substantial claim overlap (C34-C35, C58, C74) on the main conclusion about D4 limitations. OpenEval rated SUPPORTED but noted conclusion somewhat overstated. Peer reviewers rated SUPPORTED, agreeing authors 'raise several valid concerns' and the work provides 'timely and clarifying contribution.' Both accept the overall conclusion with OpenEval being slightly more critical about overstatement.

Shared claims (C70-C72) on cholesterol flip-flop kinetics and D4 binding artifacts. OpenEval rated SUPPORTED based on cited literature showing rapid flip-flop and perturbation by D4 binding. Peer reviewers also rated SUPPORTED, accepting these theoretical considerations without challenge. Strong agreement on this fundamental limitation.

Shared claims (C55-C57) on biological context for cholesterol distribution and flip-flop kinetics. OpenEval rated SUPPORTED based on biological principles and literature. Peer reviewers also rated SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting these considerations as part of valid concerns. Agreement on theoretical framework.

Shared claims (C21-C23, C31-C32) on phospholipid composition effects from Figure 1A. OpenEval rated SUPPORTED, finding experimental design appropriate with direct data support. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN, acknowledging 'valid point' but criticizing lack of binding isotherms at multiple D4 concentrations. Significant disagreement: OpenEval accepts evidence as sufficient, peer reviewers require additional quantitative data.

Shared claims (C28-C29, C31, C63-C64) on acyl chain unsaturation effects from Figure 1B. OpenEval rated SUPPORTED with direct experimental support. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN for overlapping claims in R1, requesting binding isotherms to distinguish accessibility from Kd changes. Disagreement on sufficiency: OpenEval finds data adequate, peer reviewers want saturation curves.

Shared claims (C15-C16, C25-C27, C60-C62) on mechanistic explanation of cholesterol shielding. OpenEval rated SUPPORTED based on experimental data combined with literature. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN for the broader set of claims in R1, requesting binding isotherms. Partial disagreement: OpenEval accepts mechanism as well-supported by literature, peer reviewers want more quantitative validation.

Shared claims (C45-C47) on protein interference from Figure 1C. OpenEval rated SUPPORTED with appropriate experimental design. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN, acknowledging 'valid concern' but finding discussion 'not compelling' regarding implications for Liu et al.'s microinjection approach. Disagreement on interpretation: OpenEval accepts inference to live cells, peer reviewers question relevance to Liu et al.'s methodology.

Shared claims (C36, C43-C44) on cytosolic protein concentrations and weak affinity significance. OpenEval rated SUPPORTED based on literature and experimental data. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN for overlapping claims, noting the discussion was 'not compelling' and that transient transfection may be harder to control than microinjection. Disagreement on strength of argument.

Shared claims (C49-C51) on mCherry-D4 plasma membrane localization. OpenEval rated SUPPORTED with direct microscopy data but noted unexplained differences between mCherry and DAN variants. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN, noting 'modest impact' since transfected D4 binding was previously reported, questioning why transfected protein would 'behave more correctly' than microinjected, and requesting quantitative comparison. Disagreement: OpenEval accepts data as supportive, peer reviewers question interpretation and novelty.

Shared claims (C37-C40) on DAN tag hypothesis for discrepancy with Liu et al. OpenEval rated UNCERTAIN, noting hypothesis is plausible but speculative without direct testing. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN for overlapping claims in R3, expressing concern about cell-to-cell variation and questioning whether mCherry-D4 behaves differently from DAN-D4. Agreement that interpretation is uncertain and requires validation.

Shared claims (C41-C42, C65) on DAN tag increasing protein binding affinity. OpenEval rated UNCERTAIN, noting mechanism is speculative without direct testing. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN, finding discussion 'not compelling' about protein interference implications. Agreement that this hypothesis lacks sufficient experimental support.

Shared claim (C30) on limitations in Liu et al.'s methodology. OpenEval rated SUPPORTED as fair critique with experimental support. Peer reviewers rated SUPPORTED for the broader conclusion, agreeing authors raise 'valid concerns.' Agreement on validity of critique.

Shared claim (C19) on contradictory findings from literature. OpenEval rated SUPPORTED as accurate description of limitations. Peer reviewers rated SUPPORTED but cautioned authors to 'not mischaracterize Liu et al.' since they did test some inner leaflet lipids. Agreement on general point with peer reviewers requesting more precise characterization.

OpenEval evaluated claims C67, C69, C73 on balanced conclusions about D4 having valid uses requiring rigorous interpretation, rating as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific concluding remarks.

Peer reviewers evaluated claims C3-C5, C14, C19 on characterization of Liu et al.'s approach, rating SUPPORTED but cautioning against mischaracterization since Liu et al. did test some inner leaflet lipids. No direct corresponding OpenEval result, though R11 partially overlaps with C19.
